claim: ECHO is a symmetric excitatory/inhibitory network over propositions from seven principles; it settles in about 50-210 cycles on the author's cases.
agent_test: Build the proposition graph with an LLM, run a settle loop in code, compare chosen hypothesis to LLM-only pick at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Coherence maximisation is NP-hard but approximable: SDP gives >=0.878 of optimal; greedy local flip matches ECHO on the authors' examples.
agent_test: Run exact/greedy solver vs one-shot LLM verdict on small hand-built graphs; log satisfied weight.

claim: ECHO matches known verdicts on retrodicted legal cases (Chambers, von Bulow trial 1 and 2, Vincennes) but input was coded by the author with outcome knowledge, so this is retrodiction, not validation. Thagard himself conceded in his 1989 reply that the ECHO analyses are not good tests of psychological validity.
agent_test: Have blind coders build graphs from case text without outcomes; measure intercoder agreement and verdict match.

claim: Pure explanatory coherence and a Bayes net both predicted guilt in Simpson, contrary to the acquittal; fixing it needed tuned valence or presumption-of-innocence parameters set after the verdict.
agent_test: Test an explicit burden/threshold parameter on cases where coherent story and legal standard diverge.

claim: ECHO and Bayes net give the same verdict on von Bulow trial 1, but the Bayes arm used guessed probabilities, so the comparison shows effort, not accuracy.
agent_test: Compare at equal tokens: LLM-elicited Bayes vs LLM-elicited coherence graph.

claim: ECHO encoding freedom (programmer types propositions and links; intercoder reliability untested; critics say 'explains' is undefined) is the main validity threat. LLM graph reconstruction on synthetic propositions is perfect only about half the time on sparse graphs (o1/3/4-mini); real-case variance across builds is unmeasured.
agent_test: Measure variance of verdict across independent LLM graph builds of the same case.

claim: People shift evidence ratings toward their leaning verdict (coherence shift) in legal and choice tasks. Founding numbers: Holyoak and Simon 1999 Exp 1 N=54 (48 analysed), verdict x test F(1,44)=35.3, posttest Q 1.42 v -1.56; Simon et al. 2001 N=50/125/166, F up to 78.6; Qiao et al. 2026 (new sample, N=130) F(1,128)=96.31. Also Glockner and Lee and Holyoak (N=58 snack choice, beta -0.247). No effect sizes are reported in the founding papers; baseline groups already differed (.80 of 2.55 in Simon 2001).
agent_test: Rate evidence blind, then after verdict, and again blind in a fresh context; count drift.

claim: Coherence shifts have a non-dissonance rival: predecisional distortion (Russo) and context-sensitivity. Network models and consistency-drive accounts are hard to separate on verdicts alone.
agent_test: Compare shift size with and without the model authoring the commitment.

claim: Parallel constraint satisfaction fits intuitive and deliberate human inference best (50-60% of participants), with deliberation lengthening time (d=0.85) but not changing the strategy.
agent_test: Does extra thinking budget change the LLM's decision rule or only its latency?

claim: In legal-style tasks people search mostly for disconfirming information, yet still show strong coherence shifts.
agent_test: Not tested; abstract only.

claim: A MaxSAT/factor-graph solver over an LLM's own claims raises consistency by about 10-25 points and accuracy by about 2-17 points on pre-2023 models (BeliefBank ~69->~86 F1 incl. +16.5 solver alone; ConCoRD +5 pts ConVQA, +1.4 to +1.9 F1 on NQ; Maieutic 72.5 vs 61.4 self-consistency).
agent_test: Extract claims plus entail/contradict links, solve in code, compare to majority vote at equal tokens on a frontier model.

claim: Gains depend on link quality: NLI-detected links beat gold constraints on BeliefBank but gold is better on ConVQA and NQ; the link detector is the bottleneck.
agent_test: Compare LLM-judged links vs NLI-judged links vs oracle links.

claim: Relevant-feedback context alone gives less than the solver (BeliefBank Relevant-FB 79.5 vs Constraints 85.8 F1 at batch 10).
agent_test: Prompt-only 'recall prior beliefs' vs code solver.

claim: Solvers can hurt when many weak, wrong constraints outweigh one strong true belief (rat/cat example); no error rate reported. REFLEX reports flat accuracy (79.4 to 79.9, 74.0 to 75.0, 80.2 to 80.0) with consistency up 8-11 points, so correct and wrong flips cancel; still no flip-to-wrong rate.
schema_part: G (do not let weak links outvote strong evidence)
agent_test: Inject wrong constraints and measure flip-to-wrong rate.

claim: Coherence does not guarantee truth: phlogiston and similar theories were highly coherent; LLMs also write consistent explanations equally for right and wrong options.
agent_test: Check whether logical-consistency score separates correct from incorrect explanations on a frontier model.

claim: Explanation-feature scoring (parsimony, hedging, coherence) selects the right causal explanation up to 77% on COPA/E-CARE, 17 points over GPT-3.5 judge; hedging was strongest single predictor.
agent_test: Re-run IBE-style features on current models; both papers share the same authors.

claim: Argumentation-graph solvers on LLM arguments give accuracy comparable to CoT, not better; gain is contestability.
agent_test: Compare ArgLLM-style scoring vs CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Solver-over-formalisation helps on strict deduction (Logic-LM +39.2 over standard, +18.4 over CoT) but not everywhere (ProntoQA CoT 98.79 > Logic-LM 83.20). 2025-26 update (VERGE, SMT with repair, Sonnet 3.7): FOLIO CoT 70.4, SC 72.4, Logic-LM 71.6, VERGE 87.9; but PoT beats it on ProofWriter (98.2 v 93.0).
agent_test: Do not route all problems to the solver; route by task type.

claim: Frozen-model coherence can be pushed into training (deductive closure training +3-26%); not usable in a scaffold, but its contradiction-detection step is.
agent_test: n/a

claim: LLMs show coherence-shift-like behaviour (GPT-4o Putin essays d=2.16 and 1.80; choice moderation d=0.98), but a rival account says it is context-window sensitivity independent of authorship. Cummins et al. varied authorship with matched content (chat, API, single monologue): valence effect in all three; Ns not stated.
agent_test: Rate evidence in a fresh context after verdict and compare to pre-verdict rating.

claim: LLMs given adversarial legal roles omit more unfavourable facts; balancing instructions do not remove it (human check: <20% vs 100% favour, kappa 0.47).
agent_test: Summarise the same case from neutral vs advocate framing and score fact inclusion.

claim: No study found testing ECHO or a Thagard-style network on an LLM-built evidence graph for legal verdicts, or measuring LLM coherence shift on legal evidence with pre/post ratings in the same versus a fresh context (re-searched 2026-11-10: still none). Nearest: Huntsman and Thomas 2025 (graph reconstruction, synthetic), VERGE 2026 (SMT on formal logic), Ambati 2026 (MaxSAT proposal, no results). Absence is not proven.
agent_test: This is the key untested gap.

claim: The coherence shift survives a 1-week gap between pretest and case (N=19, F(1,17)=7.71) and appears with no decision task at all (memorise N=125 F(2,236)=59.1; comprehend N=166 F(2,302)=78.6), so it is a comprehension process, not only post-decision dissonance.
agent_test: Rate evidence in a fresh context holding only the pre-rating; compare drift with same-context drift.

claim: When evidence strength is measured as likelihood ratios instead of agreement, shifts are not reliably verdict-aligned (Qiao et al. 2026, N=209 in Studies 2a-b; three-way interaction p=.083 and p=.44), while agreement ratings shift strongly (N=130, F=96.31). A constraint network fit group means at r=.79-.87.
agent_test: Compare drift when the agent gives free-text agreement versus a numeric likelihood ratio.

claim: LLMs can rebuild a known signed coherence graph from propositions in one prompt: o1/3/4-mini perfect on about half of sparse graphs, claude-3.5-sonnet and QwQ-32B also strong; benchmark is synthetic (76 graphs, 5-23 propositions) and tells nothing about variance across builds of a real case.
agent_test: Build the graph for a real case 3 times; report edge overlap and verdict agreement.

claim: The solver step is limited by formalisation quality: on FOLIO only 76.7% of unanimous formalisations are faithful (56.0% when not unanimous), 23.3% of unanimous ones still disagree with gold, and models near 20B produce valid SMT only about 30% of the time; cross-family disagreement catches 94.1% of bad formalisations at 28.8% precision.
agent_test: Log formalisation agreement across two models; fall back to CoT when they disagree.

claim: Thagard conceded in 1989 that his ECHO analyses are not good tests of psychological validity, and the only human-data check he cites (Ranney and Thagard 1988, two protocol cases) is not independent; no independently opened replication of ECHO on human confidence data was found.
agent_test: Do not claim ECHO is validated on human data.

claim: Across BeliefBank, ConCoRD and REFLEX, consistency gains from a solver are larger than accuracy gains (REFLEX consistency +8 to +11, accuracy -0.2 to +1.0); consistency is not truth.
agent_test: Report consistency and accuracy separately for any solver step.
